answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive in time, not just in count. Each new agent must complete a chain of sequential, verifiable tasks whose proofs cannot be parallelised across fake copies: a thousand clones still need a thousand chains of real work. Like a juniper rooting slowly on thin soil, influence grows only with proven history, staying small until sustained honest service lifts it toward the zenith. If one identity cheats, its proof chain is revoked, and the ripple invalidates dependent work, so mass fakery costs more than it earns.
